text: Let (Omega,F,mu) be a probability space with a filtration (F_k). Let X_k be integrable real increments, measurable at F_(k+1), with |X_k|<=b almost surely, b>0, and E[X_k|F_k]=0. Fix 0<lam0<lam1<3/b, let rho be the uniform probability measure on [lam0,lam1], and fix delta>0. Define S_n=sum_(k<n) X_k. Let V_k be nonnegative real, F_k-measurable proxies satisfying E[X_k^2|F_k]<=V_k almost surely. Put W_n=sum_(k<n) V_k. Then the probability that, for some n>0, integral exp(lambda*S_n - lambda^2*W_n/(2*(1-b*lambda/3))) d rho(lambda) reaches or exceeds 1/delta is at most delta.

scope: This is a bounded-increment predictable-variance specialization of the method of mixtures, not the entire paper, not its empirical sample-variance theorem, and not an optimized-width confidence sequence.
